items.project_definition: A synchronization gate ensuring all blocking infrastructure is verified before parallel feature development commences.
The core shared infrastructure layer containing serialization, storage resolution, and dispatch logic required by all subsequent features.
The high-level functional objective that a specific user story must satisfy to be considered complete.
A sequential numeric identifier assigned to each task entity to enable unique referencing and targeted mutation.
The lightweight data-interchange format used for persistent storage in ~/.todos.json and for scriptable output.
The minimum viable product consisting of the ability to create and mark tasks as finished.
The structural grouping of implementation units by user story to ensure independent testability.
The set of mandatory design documents including plan, spec, research, data-model, and command contracts.
The primary documentation file detailing command-line usage and persistence behavior.
The initial phase involving package skeleton creation, directory structuring, and pyproject.toml configuration.
The specific implementation unit responsible for providing a clear user message when the task collection is empty.
The verification suite organized into unit and integration directories, validated via quickstart smoke tests.
The process of assigning the created_at timestamp during the instantiation of a new task entity.
The operational command that purges all entities marked as finished from the persistent store.
The operational command that retrieves and displays all stored entities in either human-readable or machine-parseable formats.
A blocking constraint indicating that no feature work can proceed until the foundational infrastructure is fully implemented.
